summary: Independent targeted refresh on production commit 4e9fc9a confirms the reviewer-blocking reveal replay defect is fixed across observer, keyboard-focus, and initially reduced-motion completion paths, but UI-001 cannot pass because the integrated app renders blank when IntersectionObserver is unavailable even though the isolated ScrollReveal fallback remains final across motion changes.

cd frontend && node --input-type=module -e '<production Playwright audit: observer completion, keyboard-focus completion, initially reduced-motion mount, effective-motion on/off transitions, and per-variant observe-call counts>'
cd frontend && npx vitest run tests/.ui001-fallback-toggle.test.tsx --reporter=verbose (temporary independent test removed after execution)
cd frontend && node --input-type=module -e '<production Playwright no-IntersectionObserver diagnostic with pageerror and body/reveal inspection>'
python3 scripts/agentctl.py scope check UI-001 tester
tests.notes: Reviewed exact production commit 4e9fc9af819335256b1c721db342f16e57281635 and diff 68b0c8f..4e9fc9a. The focused ScrollReveal suite passed 5/5. The exact production build passed after transforming 8,481 modules. In the production browser, observer-completed patient/staff/caregiver cards remained [revealed, revealed, revealed] after Reduce motion was enabled and then disabled; observe counts stayed patient=1, staff=1, caregiver=1, workflow=3, saas=4, proving no hiding, re-observation, or replay. A patient card completed by keyboard focus also remained revealed through the same toggle sequence with identical observe counts. Instances mounted under OS reduced motion remained [visible, visible, visible] after switching to no-preference and recorded zero reveal observe calls. A temporary isolated component test passed 1/1 and proved a ScrollReveal mounted without IntersectionObserver stays visible through reduced-motion on/off rerenders; that temporary file was removed. The integrated production fallback nevertheless fails: defining window.IntersectionObserver as unavailable before navigation emits TypeError: IntersectionObserver is not a constructor from the compiled app, leaves body text empty, and produces zero reveal nodes. Source inspection identifies unguarded constructors in ContinuityField.tsx and RideMap.tsx. Prior comprehensive dock/layout/SaaS/workspace/Maria/caregiver evidence remains applicable because 68b0c8f..4e9fc9a changes only ScrollReveal, its focused tests, and the frontend report, but it cannot override this explicit fallback acceptance failure. Human approval of the motion feel is recorded and does not substitute for the failed technical fallback gate.

blockers: Integrated no-IntersectionObserver fallback: before page load, set window.IntersectionObserver to undefined and navigate to the production build. The app throws TypeError: IntersectionObserver is not a constructor, renders an empty body, and creates no reveal nodes because ContinuityField and RideMap construct IntersectionObserver without availability guards. Add narrow guards that keep ContinuityField static and RideMap on its existing static fallback when the API is unavailable; do not change normal supported-browser motion behavior.
notes_for_next_agent: The original review blocker is resolved: completed ScrollReveal instances are monotonic for the mounted session and do not hide, re-observe, or replay when effective motion changes.
Keep the fix narrow: guard the ContinuityField and RideMap observer setup, retain their static/offscreen-safe fallbacks, and add one integrated no-IntersectionObserver browser regression.

After the guard lands, rerun the focused ScrollReveal suite, exact production build, production no-observer fallback check, and the motion-toggle browser audit; unaffected prior comprehensive journey and responsive evidence can still be reused.
